title: Data Center Gas Plants to Boost US Power Emissions by 20%
source_used: Bloomberg analysis as carried by Fortune (18 Aug 2026)
key_facts: 99 proposed plants tracked by BloombergNEF would emit about 318 million metric tons of CO2 a year at industry-standard running rates, per a Bloomberg News analysis.
The US electric power industry emitted about 1,485 million metric tons last year (EIA), so the plants could lift power-sector emissions by 20 percent, and by as much as a third if run flat out.
The estimate rests on 126 gigawatts of planned on-site gas generation tracked by BloombergNEF, assuming use between 60 percent and 100 percent.
The projects are spread across 22 states and more than a third are in Texas.
Not all the proposed plants are likely to be built; some are phantom projects or long shots.

Amazon's 8,000-acre Pecos County, Texas site and a Chevron-built gas plant for Microsoft could together produce over 10 gigawatts and emit up to 45 million metric tons of CO2 equivalent a year, per regulatory filings.
Amazon and Microsoft say their climate goals have not changed.
quote_evidence: Ninety-nine proposed plants tracked by BloombergNEF would emit about 318 million metric tons of carbon dioxide annually if run at industry-standard rates, according to a Bloomberg News analysis.
Not all of the proposed plants in the BNEF data are likely to be built.

why_it_matters_hint: Gas plants built beside data centers could add about a fifth to US power-sector emissions and strain tech firms' climate pledges.
